## Tips & gotchas

- Grind down the 1/4-inch bolts so they barely touch the fabric. [t451]
- [Partial] Tap holes to avoid needing nuts for a flush look. [t451]
- [Partial] Angle the drill so the hole is hidden behind the removed light. [t451]
- Ensure the lip of the steel bar doesn't stick out too far or it will interfere with the headlamp fitment. [t451]
- Adjust for different mount lengths as they vary by model. [t451]
- Use clamps to press the bar in further if needed after installation. [t451]
- Wedge an inch off the tip of the bar to create a cretin lip that matches the interior curve. [t451]
- Do test fits and tweak the shape to your liking before finalizing. [t451]
- Tap into the stock fuse box at the end of the run. [t451]
- Use a mini-fuse for connection points. [t451]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Drilling too deep and hitting the ceiling fabric without angling correctly. [t451]
- [Partial] Forgetting to move the mirror, resulting in poor visibility or damaged glass. [t451]
- [Partial] Not test-fitting the curved steel piece before finalizing the cut. [t451]
- [Partial] Choosing a mount location that conflicts with existing sunglasses holders (on later models). [t451]
